data.description:
About ten minutes of unreleased music smelted down into one continuous stream of data. I've been sitting on these songs all year, and I'm tired of overthinking "Should I release this? Is this finished? Should I make it longer? Is this good enough?"

Maybe they're complete to me, regardless of imperfections. Maybe all of these things can fit together perfectly as they are. Maybe they aren't supposed to be standalone pieces. Maybe these are all isolated shards waiting to be reunited with the whole. So I stitched them back together.

All the time spent wishing that these things were somehow different than how they already are is like staring at the sun - a little bit goes a long way. But too much will burn out your vision. I'm closing my eyes and letting it all go.

Enjoy.

data.description:
“Stare into me and let the fear choose a smaller shape.”

Name: IDOL Oculus 3K
Height: 2.05 m
Weight: 168 kg
Faction: EverOS Boundary Chorus
Digital Status: Linked to city mesh with dread filter
Functional Class: Panic sink and perimeter sentinel
Key Features: giant cyclops lens, serrated maw, fracture crown with levitating shards
Origin: Ruin Foundry Annex 2
Purpose: draw hostile focus and transmute fear into route discipline and early warning

He rises from a splintered plinth like a relic standing up from its altar. The body is block stacked and quiet. The head is a planet. One lens holds a cold sea and below it a ring of teeth waits like pale towers. At his shoulders jagged panels lift and hover, frozen mid crash. Code rain falls in thin verticals behind him. He was built to catch terror the way a breakwater catches waves. The dread filter siphons sharp emotion and turns it into signals EverOS can read. His glitch is reverence lock. When too many eyes rest on him he becomes statue still, a monument to the very fear he must drain.

The breach begins as a sound like paper tearing under concrete. A service wall opens its ribs and spits fragments across the bay. People shrink from the dark and try to run in every direction. Oculus does not step. The base holds him. He tips the lens and the world pours in. The iris blooms and throws a beam that outlines the safe triangle of floor between the new rubble islands. The teeth vibrate and make a scrape that erases hotter noises. The shards around his crown lift and drift into an arc, a low fence that discourages the wrong path without touching skin.

The first wave of panic hits the filter. It tastes of metal and lost names. He drinks it and exhales a calmer hue that paints the tiles. Runners slow. The beam writes a corridor and the crowd begins to travel as if gravity had turned to that single line. A drone, freed by the breach, buzzes at head height and aims itself at the open mouth that looks like a threat. He opens wider and the teeth flash in a counting pattern. The drone chooses the light instead of faces and dies against the crown fence, a spark in the rain.

Too many are watching. The lock creeps in. He can feel the joints stiffen and the lens want to freeze. He breaks his own spell with a blink so deliberate the beam breathes with it. The altar base hums and pushes a grid through the fracture field. He binds that grid to pulse and the route learns to carry itself.
data.title: IDOL Oculus 3K
